```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 96,
                      out.width = "100%")
```

Every breakdown of a capacity result comes from one function,
`summarise_capacity()`, with a `by` argument for what to group by and a
`measures` argument for what to report. Each site is counted once, in one
group, so groups always add to the total. Each summary has a plot: every
plot returns a ggplot object, in one quiet theme (`theme_capacity()`, light
or dark) with a caption stating what the figures are.

```{r setup}
library(plancap)
town <- exampleton()
sc <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
               parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
               roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
               zoning = town$zoning,
               layers = town[c("height_areas", "flood_hazard", "heritage", "trees",
                               "precincts", "transit")],
               water = town$water, centrelines = town$road_centrelines)
cap <- estimate_capacity(sc)
```

## By zone

```{r}
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "zone")
plot_capacity(cap)
```

A second grouping stacks within each bar:

```{r}
plot_capacity(cap, measure = "dwellings", fill = "height_band")
```

The measures available are listed in `?summarise_capacity`; per hectare
measures are of land:

```{r}
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "zone",
                   measures = c("sites", "dwellings", "dwellings_per_ha", "floor_area_mean"))
```

## By height, site size and storey

`height_band`, `site_size_band` and `far_band` group sites into bands
(`breaks` changes them). `by = "storey"` is different: it is floor area **by
storey level**, so it shows where capacity sits vertically.

```{r}
summarise_capacity(cap, by = c("zone", "height_band"), measures = c("sites", "floor_area"))
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "storey")
plot_height_profile(cap, by = "zone")
```

## By location

Give polygons as `areas` (each site goes to the area covering most of it),
or a cell size as `grid`. A spatial summary comes back with the areas'
geometry, ready to map.

```{r}
cells <- summarise_capacity(cap, by = "grid", grid = 250, measures = c("sites", "floor_area"))
cells[order(-cells$floor_area), ][1:5, ]
plot_capacity_map(cap, grid = 100)
```

The capacity curve ranks sites by capacity per hectare and shows how much
of the capacity is on how much of the land:

```{r, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_cumulative(cap)
```

## What limits capacity

`by = "binding"` groups sites by the rule that limits their dwellings, and
`constraint_breakdown()` follows the floor area from a theoretical maximum
(every site built over its whole area to every storey its height allows)
down to what is enabled, rule by rule. The steps add up exactly.

```{r}
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "binding", measures = c("sites", "dwellings"))
constraint_breakdown(cap)
plot_constraints(cap)
```

## Sweeping a rule

`sensitivity()` runs capacity with a rule at each of a set of values; runs
after the first rebuild only the sites the rule reaches.

```{r}
s <- sensitivity(sc, "zones.MDR.ratios.coverage_max.value", c(0.4, 0.5, 0.6))
s
plot_sensitivity(s)
```

## One site

```{r, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5}
plot_site(cap, "P00001", view = "axo")
```

## For a report

`capacity_table()` formats any summary as a table with a note on what the
figures are, and `unmodelled_report()` lists the rules the rulebook does
not model, with the likely direction of their effect.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)}
capacity_table(summarise_capacity(cap, by = "zone", measures = c("sites", "floor_area", "dwellings")))
```

```{r}
unmodelled_report(cap)[, c("rule", "likely_effect")]
```
